topic: the 1919 Boston Molasses Flood -- a wave of molasses that moved faster than people could run and killed 21
title: The Wave That Killed 21 People -- And It Wasn't Water
description: AI-narrated history commentary: the true story of the 1919 Boston Molasses Flood, when a burst storage tank released 2.3 million gallons of molasses in a wave that outran people in the street.

hook_candidates.text: A wave of molasses once moved faster than people could run, and killed them.
You think a deadly flood has to be water. In 1919, Boston's was 2 million gallons of molasses.
What if a wave of dessert syrup could outrun you and kill 21 people?
In 1919, a giant steel tank in Boston burst, and what poured out wasn't water.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks flood disasters only happen with water, because they want to prove a wave of dessert syrup once killed 21 people.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a wave that killed people had to be water, not something as harmless-sounding as molasses.
closing_comment: The wave of molasses that killed 21 people in Boston moved faster than most people can actually run.

sources.note: Confirms 2.3 million gallons, 35mph wave speed, 21 deaths, rushed wartime tank construction.
Confirms fatalities, injuries, and the investigation finding the tank inadequate.

beats.text: **Molasses** wave that killed people faster than they could run.

beats.text: In 1919, a giant steel tank in Boston simply gave way.
beats.broll_query: a tall rusted steel storage tank cracking apart in an old industrial waterfront district, dramatic light

beats.text: It released 2.3 million gallons of molasses into the streets at once.

a stack of pancakes on a plate being buried under an absurd flood of dark syrup

beats.text: The wave wasn't slow or gentle, it moved faster than most people can sprint.
beats.broll_query: a person in 1919 clothing sprinting in terror down a cobblestone street away from a dark wave

beats.text: Witnesses clocked it near **35 miles** per hour, tall as a two-story building.
beats.broll_query: a towering wall of dark syrup rising two stories high above small vintage houses

beats.text: Traffic tickets didn't apply to syrup.

beats.text: Twenty-one people died, and drowning wasn't even the main cause.

beats.text: Many victims **suffocated**, pinned under syrup too thick to escape.

beats.text: Sticky really is the wrong word.

beats.text: The company rushed the tank's construction for wartime demand, and investigators proved it should have never held anything.
